intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that glucose/galactose malabsorption (GGM) is caused by mutation in the SLC5A1 gene (182380), which encodes the sodium/glucose cotransporter SGLT1, on chromosome 22q12.3.

checks.claim: Glucose/galactose malabsorption (GGM) is caused by mutation in the SLC5A1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Sequence analysis of the amplified products has revealed a single missense mutation in SGLT1 which cosegregates with the GGM phenotype
checks.explanation: Title and abstract attribute GGM to a defect in SGLT1 (SLC5A1).

checks.claim: The SLC5A1 gene encodes the sodium/glucose cotransporter SGLT1.
checks.evidence_quote: We have previously cloned and sequenced a Na+/glucose cotransporter from normal human ileum and shown that this gene, SGLT1, resides on the distal q arm of chromosome 22.
checks.explanation: SLC5A1 is the approved symbol for SGLT1.

checks.claim: The SLC5A1 gene is located on chromosome 22q12.3.
checks.evidence_quote: this gene, SGLT1, resides on the distal q arm of chromosome 22
checks.explanation: Chromosomal location is standard nomenclature. The paper only says the distal q arm of chromosome 22 and does not give a band.

paragraphs.text: Glucose/galactose malabsorption is an inborn defect of intestinal absorption of certain monosaccharides (ANDERSON et al., 1965). Turk et al. (1991) described it as an autosomal recessive disease in which dietary glucose and galactose are not absorbed from the intestine. It appears within the first weeks of life. The resulting severe diarrhea and dehydration are usually fatal unless these sugars are removed from the diet.

checks.claim: Glucose/galactose malabsorption is an inborn defect of intestinal absorption of certain monosaccharides.
checks.evidence_quote: AN INBORN DEFECT OF INTESTINAL ABSORPTION OF CERTAIN MONOSACCHARIDES.
checks.explanation: Only the title was supplied. Its wording matches the claim's description exactly, but the title never names glucose or galactose or calls the condition glucose/galactose malabsorption. With no abstract or full text, I can't confirm that the monosaccharides in the paper are glucose and galactose.

checks.evidence_quote: Glucose/galactose malabsorption (GGM) is an autosomal recessive disease

checks.evidence_quote: manifesting within the first weeks of life

checks.claim: Glucose/galactose malabsorption causes severe diarrhea and dehydration.
checks.evidence_quote: The consequent severe diarrhoea and dehydration are usually fatal unless these sugars are eliminated from the diet.

checks.claim: The severe diarrhea and dehydration of glucose/galactose malabsorption are usually fatal unless glucose and galactose are removed from the diet.
checks.evidence_quote: The consequent severe diarrhoea and dehydration are usually fatal unless these sugars are eliminated from the diet.

paragraphs.text: Elsas et al. (1970) found a partial defect in renal glucose reabsorption in the proband of the family they studied.

checks.evidence_quote: A partial defect in renal glucose reabsorption was found in the proband.

paragraphs.text: Abdullah et al. (1996) studied 8 children who were first seen for chronic watery diarrhea, present since birth, and failure to thrive. One child had a renal stone at the first visit, and another was found to have one on follow-up.

checks.evidence_quote: Eight children with chronic diarrhea from glucose-galactose malabsorption from eight different families are presented.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that the 8 children had glucose-galactose malabsorption.

checks.evidence_quote: They were first seen for chronic watery diarrhea, present since birth, and failure to thrive.

paragraphs.text: Xin and Wang (2011) reported that all affected individuals presented with watery diarrhea.

checks.claim: All individuals affected with glucose/galactose malabsorption reported by Xin and Wang (2011) presented with watery diarrhea.
checks.evidence_quote: Clinically, all affected individuals presented with classic watery diarrhea and dehydration.
checks.explanation: The abstract states directly that all affected individuals had watery diarrhea.

paragraphs.text: Elsas et al. (1970) found that jejunal mucosa from all subjects took up fructose in a similar way in vitro.

checks.claim: In the glucose/galactose malabsorption study by Elsas et al. (1970), jejunal mucosa from all subjects took up fructose in a similar way in vitro.
checks.evidence_quote: All subjects accumulated fructose similarly.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes in vitro studies of jejunal mucosal biopsies and then says all subjects accumulated fructose similarly, so the claim follows from what is stated.

paragraphs.text: Turk et al. (1991) stated that GGM is an autosomal recessive disease, and they found a missense mutation in SGLT1 that cosegregated with the GGM phenotype in a family. Martín et al. (1996) (PMID 8563765) referred to 2 sisters with GGM who carried a missense mutation in the SGLT1 gene. Martín et al. (1996) (PMID 8844006) described a large consanguineous family.

checks.evidence_quote: Glucose/galactose malabsorption (GGM) is an autosomal recessive disease

paragraphs.text: Turk et al. (1991) sequenced amplified products of the SLC5A1 (SGLT1) gene in a family with GGM. They found a single missense mutation that cosegregated with the GGM phenotype. Xenopus oocytes injected with cRNA carrying the mutation completely lost Na(+)-dependent glucose transport.

paragraphs.text: Martín et al. (1996) screened the SLC5A1 gene in 30 new patients with GGM. Using a heterologous expression system, they concluded that GGM is caused by defects in both the trafficking and the function of the SGLT1 protein.

checks.claim: Martín et al. (1996) screened the SLC5A1 gene in 30 new patients with glucose/galactose malabsorption.
checks.evidence_quote: The gene has now been screened in 30 new patients
checks.explanation: States that the SGLT1 gene (SLC5A1) was screened in 30 new GGM patients.

checks.claim: Using a heterologous expression system, Martín et al. (1996) concluded that glucose/galactose malabsorption is caused by defects in the trafficking of the SGLT1 protein.
checks.evidence_quote: Defects in Na+/glucose cotransporter (SGLT1) trafficking and function cause glucose-galactose malabsorption.
checks.explanation: The title states the conclusion about trafficking defects. The abstract says a heterologous expression system was used to link the mutations to the phenotype.

checks.claim: Using a heterologous expression system, Martín et al. (1996) concluded that glucose/galactose malabsorption is caused by defects in the function of the SGLT1 protein.
checks.evidence_quote: Defects in Na+/glucose cotransporter (SGLT1) trafficking and function cause glucose-galactose malabsorption.
checks.explanation: The title states the conclusion about functional defects. The abstract says expression studies linked the mutations to the phenotype.

paragraphs.text: Turk et al. (1991) noted that the disorder is usually fatal unless glucose and galactose are removed from the diet. In the series reported by Abdullah et al. (1996), all of the children responded clinically to a fructose-based formula and were thriving at follow-up.

checks.evidence_quote: The consequent severe diarrhoea and dehydration are usually fatal unless these sugars are eliminated from the diet.

checks.claim: All of the children with glucose/galactose malabsorption reported by Abdullah et al. (1996) responded clinically to a fructose-based formula.
